description: In 1818, 18-year-old Mary Shelley wrote the first major science fiction novel. Victor Frankenstein creates life, then flees his creature: a fable about science without ethics.

hero.hook: A stormy night, a bet between poets, and the myth of the modern Prometheus.

blocks.text: Published in **1818**, **Frankenstein or the Modern Prometheus** is considered the first major **science fiction** novel. **Mary Shelley** was only **18 years old** when she wrote it, at the crossroads of  noir and the scientific debates of her time. **[[Romanticism]]**

Victor Frankenstein and his nameless being are not just gothic horror characters. They ask a lasting question: what happens to a consciousness that we create, then abandon? The novel questions the : we cannot create a life without taking responsibility for its aftermath. **[[The responsibility of the creator (modern Prometheus)]]**

In **1816**, the eruption of the **Tambora** volcano in Indonesia plunged Europe into a : gray skies, lost crops, apocalyptic atmosphere. Mary Shelley is staying at **Villa Diodati** on Lake Geneva with **Percy Shelley** and **Lord Byron**. To relieve boredom, Byron offers a scary story competition. **[[Year without summer (1816)]]**

blocks.caption: Mary Shelley, author of a myth that goes far beyond Gothic horror.
Villa Diodati: birth of Frankenstein in the storm of 1816.

blocks.text: John Polidori, Byron's doctor, also wrote the founding text of the modern vampire in Diodati, before Dracula.

Mary Shelley is inspired by , these experiments which seemed to awaken the muscles of corpses. In a daydream, she sees a student in front of a creature that comes to life before her eyes. Alone among the participants, she sees the bet through to the end and produces a masterpiece. **[[Galvanism]]**

sections.title: The Lake Geneva laboratory: an apocalyptic genesis

blocks.text: **Victor Frankenstein** embodies : ambition that defies the natural order. In **Ingolstadt**, he seeks the “secret of life”, not to get rich, but to become a **Modern Prometheus**, like the Greek titan who stole fire from the gods. When his creature wakes up, the dream immediately turns into a nightmare. **[[Hubris]]**

blocks.caption: Shelley's creature: terrifying, but above all eloquent and conscious.

blocks.text: Victor flees in disgust at the ugliness of what he has created. He abandons his artificial “son”: it is this cowardice, more than the act of creation itself, which triggers the tragedy. Shelley shows that a science without conscience condemns the creator as much as the rejected creature.

The originality of the novel lies in the voice of the creature. Intelligent and eloquent, she learned by observing a family of farmers and reading  by **Milton**. Born “good” according to the , she sees herself corrupted by the violent rejection of men. **[[Paradise Lost]]** **[[Tabula rasa]]**
I am bad because I am unhappy.

She asks for a companion so that she no longer suffers alone; Victor refuses out of fear. So she destroys everything he loves to reduce him to his own solitude. The novel becomes a reflection on : society sometimes creates its monsters by excluding those who are different. **[[Social determinism]]**

sections.title: The Awakening of the Creature: A Nameless Consciousness

blocks.text: The novel ends in the **Arctic**, Victor dead, the creature disappearing into the mists promising to annihilate itself. Today, “Frankenstein” refers to any technology that escapes its inventor: GMOs, artificial intelligence, genetic engineering. Shelley anticipates . **[[Posthumanism]]**
In popular culture, the monster is often referred to as “Frankenstein”. In reality, Frankenstein is the creator: the being has no name, a sign of Victor's denial of paternity.
**Frankenstein** reminds us that we cannot create a life without taking responsibility for its aftermath. The real monster is not ugliness, but the abandonment of what we gave birth to.

sections.title: A modern myth and its universal posterity
